reference: Documented fw dry-run contracts with independently encoded nftables/iptables argument text. No matching GNU fw CLI exists.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata availability and the documented fw synopsis
nft dry-run filter rule construction with source, destination, interface, conntrack state, multiport, and rate match fields
iptables dry-run IPv6 deny rule construction with multiport and reject mode
nft dry-run DNAT and masquerade rule construction
relative-file restore and save dry-run output for nft and iptables backends
line-oriented batch parsing in nft dry-run mode
Pure backend private-store flush effects and absent-chain idempotence, independently checked without any kernel firewall backend.
exclusions: No live nft, iptables, ip6tables, ipset, kernel ruleset, or network operation is run; those require a disposable VM or independently reviewed privileged mock.
The dry-run cases verify generated command text only and do not establish that a host firewall accepts or applies those commands.
The binary exposes no GNU-compatible fw reference command, so fw behavior is tested as a documented contract rather than falsely labeled GNU parity.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash registers fw as a loadable builtin through PATH-independent type metadata.
Verify the builtin help metadata is available to Bash help without depending on external programs.
Check documented nft dry-run argv construction and ordering for the common filter match fields; -n must print argv without running nft.
cases.script: fw -n -B nft allow 198.51.100.7 -D 203.0.113.4 -p tcp --multiport 80,443 -i eth0 --ct-state new,established --limit 10/minute
cases.stdout: nft add rule inet fw input ip saddr 198.51.100.7 ip daddr 203.0.113.4 iifname "eth0" ct state { new,established } tcp dport { 80,443 } limit rate 10/minute accept

cases.purpose: Check the documented iptables backend dispatches an IPv6 deny rule to ip6tables and preserves multiport and tcp-reset rejection arguments in dry-run output.
cases.stdout: ip6tables -A BASHFW_IN -s 2001:db8::7 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 22,2222 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset

cases.purpose: Check documented nft dry-run command construction places DNAT in prerouting and masquerade in postrouting with their address and interface matches.
cases.script:
fw -n -B nft dnat 203.0.113.9:443 '->' 192.0.2.20:8443 -p tcp
fw -n -B nft masquerade 192.0.2.0/24 -o eth0
cases.stdout:
nft add rule inet fw prerouting ip daddr 203.0.113.9 tcp dport 443 dnat to 192.0.2.20:8443
nft add rule inet fw postrouting ip saddr 192.0.2.0/24 oifname "eth0" masquerade

cases.purpose: Check explicit relative-file restore/save dry-run forms for nft and iptables. The input file exists only in the private fixture directory; no backend executable runs.
cases.script:
printf 'fixture rules\n' > rules.conf
fw -n -B nft restore rules.conf
fw -n -B iptables restore rules.conf
fw -n -B nft save saved-nft.conf
fw -n -B iptables save saved-iptables.conf
cases.stdout:
nft -f rules.conf
iptables-restore rules.conf
save saved-nft.conf
save saved-iptables.conf

cases.purpose: Check the documented contract that an explicitly named missing restore file returns failure with a diagnostic; capture the builtin status before reporting it.
cases.script: if fw -n -B nft restore missing.rules; then printf 'fw-status=0\n'; else rc=$?; printf 'fw-status=%s\n' "$rc"; fi

cases.purpose: Check documented line-oriented batch parsing, comment skipping, and sequential nft argv output in dry-run mode without applying firewall changes.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '# sample rules' 'allow 192.0.2.1 -p tcp -d 443' 'deny 198.51.100.2' > rules.batch
fw -n -B nft batch rules.batch
cases.stdout:
nft add rule inet fw input ip saddr 192.0.2.1 tcp dport 443 accept
nft add rule inet fw input ip saddr 198.51.100.2 drop

cases.purpose: Live allow/deny, unban, flush, and reset behavior depends on a real kernel firewall ruleset and can change packet filtering.
cases.reason: No live-backend fixture exists. The VM image has iptables but not the nft CLI, so only the iptables backend can be qualified live; the nft live path stays unexercised until nftables is added.

cases.purpose: Set-backed rules and persistence require live nft/ipset backend state and a safe, independently verifiable restore target.
cases.reason: fw's set backends are ipset (iptables mode, fw.c:1527-1560) and the nft CLI (fw.c:1514-1550); the VM image contains neither, so a bounded side script cannot create or observe a live set. Dry-run set argv can be added now.

cases.purpose: Pure file-store flush removes only the selected relative private chain and is idempotent on an absent chain. This backend returns before nft/iptables/kernel operations.
cases.script:
export BASHFW_DIR=store
mkdir -p store/input store/output
printf remove > store/input/rule
printf preserve > store/output/rule
fw -B pure flush input
[[ ! -e store/input && -f store/output/rule ]]
fw -B pure flush input
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; assert Path("store/output/rule").read_bytes()==b"preserve"; print("private-store-preserved")'
